source_title: paytondevs/gen5w-preconditioning: an app that gives you a manual preconditioning button in your IONIQ 5. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
an app that gives you a manual preconditioning button in your IONIQ 5 or EV6.
hold the TUNE knob, press Start , and Launchpad asks the car to start conditioning the battery. no navigation destination needed.
this app was originally designed to be essentially a replacement for the stock headunit launcher, but it turned out to be kinda useless outside of the preconditioning and wifi settings. those parts are still there if you want them.
check the compatibility chart first. it lists every car and head-unit software version Launchpad supports right now. what matters is the head unit's software version, not the model year.
your car isn't listed? the chart also explains how to run the vehicle porting kit , a USB drive that safely reads your car's details so support can be added.
EV6 owners: start with the EV6 installation and everyday-use guide .
This process involves making unauthorized modifications to the infotainment system of your car. One wrong move can render it entirely unusable, leaving you with a very costly repair bill . Take care to never delete or modify any files in the car. If you are unsure about anything in this document , don't leave it up to chance! Feel free to DM me on Twitter or Reddit and I'll try to help.
if you aren't comfortable modifying the infotainment system of your car, a hardware mod exists that replicates this functionality in an easily reversible and safer manner.
a USB drive formatted FAT32 or exFAT . a small, empty one is easiest.
a way to reboot the headunit (the pinhole button in the climate control bar)
you don't need ADB, Wi-Fi, or a terminal.
NEMESIS is what lets us install things on the headunit. you only do this once. follow the Quick Installation Guidance in its README . In short:
download ota_package.tar (you don't need to build it yourself) and copy it to the root of the USB drive. don't extract it.
plug the drive into the car. "No Supported Files" is expected.
open Engineering Mode → USB Copy → Update DSP → Update OTA .
wait for it to install and restart the headunit. an Error 684 afterwards is expected. 651 means the file didn't extract; check the drive and try again.
to check that it worked: press the NAV button three times quickly and NEMESIS Manager should open.
once that's done, delete ota_package.tar from the drive (or use a different drive).
2. put the Launchpad installer on the drive
download Launchpad-install-usb.zip from the releases page (the newest one is at the top). it needs NEMESIS 1.16 or newer.
on an older NEMESIS, download Launchpad-manual-install-usb.zip instead. it works the same way, but its drive also has a launchpad/ folder with our install script, NEMESIS asks to run it instead of install it (one prompt, also for updates), and it writes launchpad-install.log to the drive.
don't use paytondev.launchpad.zip for this: that's the package itself, and extracting it onto the drive gives "Invalid package descriptor".
extract it so its contents sit at the root of the drive, with nothing else from NEMESIS left on it. the drive should look exactly like this:
Mac: double-clicking the zip makes a Launchpad-install-usb folder (Safari may already have done this for you). open that folder and copy everything inside it to the drive, not the folder itself.
Windows: right-click the zip → Extract All… , and change the destination to the drive itself (e.g. E:\ ). by default Windows adds a subfolder, which won't work.
don't unzip packages/paytondev.launchpad.zip . NEMESIS needs it as a zip.
if an old NEMESIS.data or NEMESIS.sh is on the drive, move it off first. the car only looks at the one NEMESIS.data in the root.
it does the same thing, and moves anything NEMESIS-related already on the drive into a NEMESIS-backup- folder instead of overwriting it.
the last argument is the folder you downloaded the zip to.
park, turn the car on, and wait for the headunit to finish starting.
plug the drive into a USB data port (the one you'd use for music or CarPlay, not a charge-only port).
NEMESIS asks whether to install the package on the USB drive. tap Yes . if Launchpad is already installed, it then asks whether to update it; tap Yes again. you have 60 seconds for each. if you miss one, unplug the drive and plug it back in.
wait for the result dialog. it usually takes a few seconds and can take up to about 20.
if the dialog says it failed, open NEMESIS Manager → Logs → Copy to USB , which writes a NEMESIS-logs folder to the drive. please include it if you ask me for help.
reboot the headunit with the pinhole button and remove the drive. once it's back up, hold the TUNE knob for about a second and Launchpad should open.
you only need the USB drive again to update.
hold TUNE to open Launchpad and go to preconditioning.
press Start . Launchpad shows Request sent while it waits for the car to say yes. if the battery is already warm, it asks you first and offers Start anyway .
when the car confirms, it shows Active . that's the only sign the battery is actually being conditioned. the car can still say no, for example if the battery is warm enough or the charge is too low.
if the car hasn't confirmed after five minutes on the EV6 (two on the IONIQ 5), Launchpad cancels the request for you. an Active session is never cut short.
press Stop to cancel, even while it's still waiting. closing Launchpad does not stop a request that's already running.
dark mode: go to Advanced → Appearance . Follow car (the default) matches the head unit's day/night display, or pick Light or Dark to keep one. Follow car uses the head unit's Day/Night display setting, including Auto. if it doesn't switch on your car, the Appearance signals panel at the bottom of Advanced shows what the head unit reports.
exactly the same as installing: put Launchpad-install-usb.zip (or Launchpad-manual-install-usb.zip on NEMESIS older than 1.16) from the newest release on the drive, run it, and reboot. if Launchpad is already installed, it updates it in place.
your favorites and settings are kept. it also works if you installed an older version over ADB. running the drive twice is harmless.
if preconditioning is running, press Stop and wait for it to end.
open NEMESIS Manager (press NAV three times) → Packages → Launchpad → Uninstall .
this removes Launchpad and its TUNE shortcut. if you installed an older version over ADB and Launchpad isn't in the Packages list, run the USB installer once first, then uninstall. NEMESIS stays installed. if you want that gone too, use Wipe NEMESIS in NEMESIS Manager. see the NEMESIS docs .
Launchpad is installed as a normal NEMESIS package, so it shows up in NEMESIS Manager → Packages , and uninstalling it from there removes everything.
it adds one file to the car's system area, /system/app/Launchpad.apk , because that's the only way Android will show the app. no Hyundai or Kia files are changed.
the installer checks everything first and puts the previous version back if anything goes wrong.
the TUNE-hold service and a copy of the app live in /data/nemesis/apps/paytondev.launchpad/ .
before writing /system/app/Launchpad.apk , the installer copies and checks everything in /data/local/tmp (cleared on reboot) and checks there's enough space. /system is made writable only for that one write and is set back to read-only right after. if the written file doesn't match, the previous version is put back.
already use ADB with your car? there are manual ADB install steps , but you don't need them.
see BUILDING.md . releases are built with tools/build_apk.sh and tools/build_usb_bundles.py .
want to fix something or add your car? see CONTRIBUTING.md .
EV6 development, documentation, and vehicle testing: Abro86 , with development, documentation, and host-test assistance from OpenAI Codex.
